data.title: The Collapse of Western Rome
sentences: The collapse of the Western Roman Empire was not a single event, but a century-long disintegration.
Decades of civil war and economic decay left the state vulnerable to external pressures.
When the Huns surged into Europe, they pushed displaced Germanic tribes directly into Roman territories.
The 378 Battle of Adrianople signaled a turning point, as Rome lost its ability to contain these migrating groups.
By 406, the Rhine frontier was breached, and by 410, Rome itself was looted by Visigoths.
Internal stability crumbled as the military became reliant on foreign mercenaries with shifting loyalties.
The loss of North Africa to the Vandals stripped the empire of its vital grain supply and tax revenue.
Political power devolved into a cycle of puppet emperors controlled by military commanders.
Finally, in 476, the chieftain Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus and refused to name a successor.
This act ended the Western line, leaving the East to survive for another millennium.
